title: Unify toggle + segmented-control interaction parity and tokenized focus scaling
creator: Asha Iyer
description: Problem: Toggle components (single switches) and segmented controls (multi-option toggles) in the design system diverge in keyboard semantics, focus treatment, and hit-target sizing across density modes. Engineers and customers have reported inconsistent focus rings, confusing keyboard expectations (space vs arrow behavior), and visual jitter when reduced-motion is enabled. Goal: Define a single interaction surface and token contract so both atoms and compound segmented controls behave predictably across densities, themes (light/dark/high-contrast), and motion preferences.
background: Current state: toggles use aria-pressed and space to toggle; segmented-controls are implemented as role=tablist or radiogroup inconsistently across apps.

Observed issues: (1) Focus ring thickness is hardcoded in CSS resulting in clip/overflow on compact components. (2) Compact density hitboxes fall below 44px touch target on mobile. (3) Reduced motion preference still shows scale/fade transitions causing perceptual issues for people with vestibular sensitivity. (4) High contrast mode loses focus visibility because focus ring uses blended token that becomes transparent with forced-color adjustments.

Related tickets: DES-85620 (nested toggle group focus), DES-114512 (credential field interactions) — these surfaced overlapping accessibility patterns but did not reconcile tokens or spacing rules across components.
acceptance_criteria: A token contract is published describing focusRingWidth, focusRingOffset, focusRingColor, interactiveHitboxPadding, and motionReduceBehavior with explicit values for default/compact/dense modes.

Toggle and segmented-control components share the same keyboard semantics doc: single-toggle uses Space/Enter to toggle; segmented-control (radiogroup) supports ArrowLeft/ArrowRight for option movement and Space/Enter to activate where appropriate; implementation guidance covers both single and grouped use cases.
All components render a visible focus state in high-contrast forced-color modes (WCAG UAAG considerations) — validated in Windows High Contrast + macOS accessibility mode.

Compact density does not reduce the effective touch target below 44x44px; interactiveHitboxPadding token is applied internally as invisible padding so visual size can remain compact but target stays accessible.
Reduced motion preference must disable scale/slide animations on toggle activation and segmented selection; only opacity crossfades allowed where necessary and documented.
Design tokens are backward-compatible: existing components using previous tokens continue to render but emit a deprecated-warning comment in the token map; migration guide included.
Design handoff artifacts (Figma frames + cross-platform code snippets) and a small implementation PR are linked and reviewed by platform engineering and accessibility engineering.
implementation_notes: Token names proposed: token.focusRing.width, token.focusRing.offset, token.focusRing.color, token.hitbox.padding, token.motion.reduced.enabled, token.density.compact.scaleFactor.
Prefer radiogroup semantics for segmented-controls when exclusive selection is required; document when role=tablist is acceptable (e.g., when selection controls view changes).
Use CSS custom properties mapped from tokens so runtime teams can override per-brand/theme without component rewrites.
Hitbox approach: use pseudo-element or ::after to extend touch area by token.hitbox.padding (pointer-events: auto); ensure no layout shift by making it position:absolute within the component root.
Focus ring: compute outline-offset using token.focusRing.offset and ensure focus ring does not cause layout overflow by applying contain:paint where supported or an inner focus ring layer.
Motion: add prefers-reduced-motion media query branch in component CSS; replace transform-based scale with opacity or instantaneous state change when reduced-motion is active.

Cross-platform QA checklist: Chrome/Edge/Safari iOS/Android (VoiceOver/TalkBack), keyboard-only navigation, screen reader announcements for toggle state and segmented selection, high-contrast forced-color verification.
Design tokens will be added to the next design-2.8 release; runtime teams to accept via token mapping PR (runtime-1.18 may need small wiring changes).
decisions: Adopt radiogroup + radio semantics as default for segmented-control to match ARIA expectations for exclusive selection and arrow-key navigation.
Standardize on Space/Enter toggling for single-switch toggles and reserve Arrow navigation for segmented groups to avoid keyboard conflicts.
Implement invisible hitbox padding token to keep visual compactness while meeting touch-target guidelines.
Focus ring will be tokenized and drawn in an inner layer to avoid layout shift and ensure consistent clipping across themes.
